question: When does the native hand a torpedo bomber its release-order budget unit+C58h, relative to the plane's spawn, the squadron's construction and the task the order installs? The host issued it only after a task existed, so arm tick 1 saw a budget of 0.
answer: The brief's premise was wrong, and so was the host's. The issue path is not free-running from mission start: 007CEA8D, the one call site of 007C0D90 in the image, sits in a stage at 007CE9FD-007CEB31 at the tail of the plane fixed step, past five guards, a randomised countdown unit+C28h and a pending-request counter unit+C20h that must be strictly positive. An exhaustive disp32 scan of .text for every instruction touching a +C20h field, reads included, finds twelve sites; the counter's one raiser is 007BBC00 ADD dword [ECX+0xC20], EBX with EBX=1 from 007BBBAB, the last instruction of 007BBBA0 BSP_Unit_RequestOrdnanceRelease before its POP EBX/RET, past all three of that function's early exits. A MOV-only store census misses it. So the flight-wide budget of 999 is issued AFTER an aircraft has requested an ordnance release, not before: unit+C58h is how a leader's drop authorises the rest of the flight, not a precondition for the first drop. The squadron block itself does exist from launch (007F2C60 from 004F0AD0), which is the one part of the brief that held.
coverage: reconstructed for the 007CE9FD stage and the 007BBC00 raiser; partial for the squadron construction (the constructor and its three callers are named from the listing, the member-array population is not read); contract: unread for the device walk vtable +1FCh, the app-state field [00E188A8]+1FE4h, unit+C3Ah, unit+5Dh and the class descriptor field +1F4h

tree_base.note: Both baselines are this tree's own before-runs at f4a96ed28, not the standing censuses, because main moved twice today.

census_method.callsite_census_007c0d90: python tools/callsite_census.py 007c0d90 - one CALL, 007CEA8D in 007CE040. rel32 and absolute dword, image wide.
census_method.callsite_census_007bbba0: python tools/callsite_census.py 007bbba0 - 34 sites; the torpedo task's own are 009D4956 (BSP_BotTaskTorpedo_TickArm), 009D258A, 009D25B3, 009D26F8, 009D2938, 009D29CB and 009D3EB6.
census_method.store_census_0x910_0xc20_0xc28: python tools/store_census.py found 22 / 3 / 1 stores. It reported 007D625B for unit+C20h and nothing else on the unit, which alone would have made the stage dead code.
census_method.exhaustive_disp_scan_0xc20: local/scan_disp.py, capstone over the .text raw bytes, sixteen alignments with resync, every operand whose memory displacement is 0xC20 with a register base, reads included: twelve sites. This is what found 007BBC00. The store census missed it because it is an ADD with a register source.
census_method.register_provenance: Filtered the whole 007CE040 listing (1092 lines, local/output/disasm-raw-007ce040-length-4402-*.txt) for every write to EDI: seven LEA/MOV sites plus the POP. The last before the stage is 007CE848 LEA EDI,[ESI-310h]; 007CEAFE MOV EDI,EDI is alignment. So EDI is the unit and ESI the element at unit+310h.

BSP_PlaneSquadronTickableEntity_Construct, body 007F2C60-007F2E18, writes the avoid-zone layer ctl+34Ch at 007F2CDB and the attack mode ctl+370h at 007F2DC1; the block is therefore live before any task
BSP_Plane_ReadPropertyBag zeroes unit+C20h with EBX from the XOR at 007D619A, and builds the device at unit+DECh at 007D61B4; unit+C28h has no writer outside 007CE040, so both start at zero
the control latch, the instruction before the stage
the release-order issue stage begins; 007CE99D's JE lands on it, so no branch skips it
the issue path, reached only with unit+C20h > 0
the raiser: every ordnance-release request adds one to unit+C20h, so the budget follows a drop
